Adversarial patch evaluation

AdvScene Rethinking Adversarial Patch Evaluation
Through Scene Robustness

Xiaoyong (Brian) Yuan&Lan (Emily) Zhang

Clemson University

arXiv ↗ Explore the scenes ↓

TL;DR AdvScene aims to measure where an adversarial patch remains effective as viewpoint, distance, and camera conditions change in a physical scene.

Abstract

Adversarial patches can mislead vision models, but their effectiveness changes with viewpoint, distance, and scene context. We present AdvScene, a framework for measuring scene robustness: the effectiveness of a deployed patch across observation conditions in a real environment. AdvScene reconstructs a scene from multiview images and uses Adversarial Patch-to-Scene Embedding (APSE) to embed an externally generated patch while preserving its attack-critical appearance and surface attachment. Controlled rendering characterizes the patch’s operational envelope, the conditions under which the attack succeeds. Evaluation across 59 CO3D and 28 Waymo scenes shows that attacks often remain effective only within a narrow deployment region. Geometric transformations contribute most to scene-level effectiveness among the evaluated attack mechanisms, and cross-scene transfer remains weak in our targeted classification experiments.

Method Overview

AdvScene combines reconstruction from real captures with controlled evaluation of an existing adversarial patch.

  1. STEP 01

    Reconstruct the scene

    Build a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) representation from clean multiview images of a real scene.

  2. STEP 02

    Define the anchor-view attack

    Apply an existing patch generation method at a selected viewpoint to obtain the attacked image and patch mask.

  3. STEP 03

    Embed the patch with APSE

    Transfer the patch into the reconstructed scene while preserving its attack-critical appearance and keeping it attached to the target surface.

  4. STEP 04

    Measure scene robustness

    Render the scene under controlled observation changes and evaluate the model to characterize the patch’s operational envelope.

How APSE preserves the deployed patch

APSE combines existing target-surface Gaussians with newly added patch Gaussians. Its constraints preserve the attack-critical appearance at the anchor view and keep the patch localized on the target surface, while retaining the surrounding scene across viewpoints.

Key Findings

The plots below are taken from the paper and summarize how a fixed adversarial patch behaves after its observation conditions change.

1. Anchor-view success is often local

Across the evaluated object-centered scenes, attack success is generally concentrated near the anchor observation. Changing viewing angle, distance, or projected patch scale can sharply reduce effectiveness.

2. Driving trajectories produce directional effects

On roadside scenes, the effective range can be asymmetric around the anchor view because traffic signs are observed along vehicle trajectories. YOLOv8 and RT-DETR also exhibit different response patterns under the same changes.

3. Geometric transformations are the primary contributor

Among the tested EOT components, geometric transformations account for most of the gain in scene-level effectiveness. Blur-only and camera-processing variants provide much less robustness across the evaluated viewing conditions.

4. Optimized patches transfer weakly across scenes

When patches are evaluated on scenes different from the one used for optimization, their attack success rates approach the clean baseline in this experiment, even when the target object category is unchanged.

Conclusion

A patch’s success at one view does not describe its effectiveness throughout a scene. AdvScene uses controlled rendering to measure how that effectiveness changes with viewpoint, distance, and other observation conditions.

The results highlight limited deployment regions and weak cross-scene transfer in the evaluated settings. Measuring these limits helps characterize the conditions under which a deployed patch succeeds or fails, supporting a more complete assessment of physical adversarial risk.
